The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Mental health services would receive investment to achieve parity with physical health, including counsellors in all schools. A National Cancer Control Plan and measures to end new HIV cases by 2030 are included.

## Social Care
The manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment for free personal care, increased carer pay with a career structure, and £3bn additional funding for children's social care. Disability benefits would increase by 5%.

## Housing
Plans include building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy
The manifesto targets wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, ending new oil and gas licences and fossil fuel subsidies, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Community ownership of energy infrastructure would be encouraged. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy
Proposed spending includes £40bn average annual investment in green economic transformation. Railways, water companies, and major retail energy companies would return to public ownership. A wealth tax of 1-2% on assets above £10m would be introduced, alongside capital gains tax reform and alignment of investment income taxation with employment income rates.

## Employment
The manifesto proposes a £15/hour minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repeal of anti-union legislation, and a four-day working week. Gig economy workers would receive full employment rights.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, the five-week benefit wait would end, and the bedroom tax would be scrapped. Carer's allowance would increase by at least 10%.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would give legal personhood to nature. 30% of land and seas would be protected by 2030. Water companies would be nationalised. A new Right to Roam Act for England is proposed.

## Education
School funding would increase by £8bn, including £2.5bn annually for building repairs. Tuition fees would be scrapped and maintenance grants restored. SEND provision would receive £5bn investment.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with railways returning to public ownership. £2.5bn annually would fund cycleways and footpaths. Free bus travel for under-18s is proposed. New petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment, creating safe asylum routes, abolishing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, and permitting asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## Foreign Policy
The party supports an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident. Overseas aid would increase to 1% of GNI by 2033.

## Funding
Revenue measures include wealth taxes, carbon taxes, and business tax reforms estimated to raise £170bn+ by 2030. Additional borrowing would fund capital investment.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Priorities

The manifesto establishes five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, breaking barriers to opportunity, and NHS reform.

## Economic Policy

Labour commits to fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt by the fifth forecast year. Corporation tax will be capped at 25%. The party pledges no increases to Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT.

Key economic initiatives include:
- A National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) for industrial investment
- An Industrial Strategy Council on statutory footing
- Business rates reform in England
- A ten-year infrastructure strategy
- Planning system overhaul to enable 1.5 million new homes
- Rail nationalisation as contracts expire
- Skills England to coordinate workforce training

## Energy and Environment

Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, will receive £8.3 billion. The target is zero-carbon electricity by 2030 through expanded wind, solar, and nuclear power. No new oil and gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing licences continue. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy efficiency upgrades.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubled CT/MRI scanners, 8,500 new mental health staff, and workforce planning. Social care will move toward a National Care Service with national standards.

Education measures include 6,500 new teachers, free primary school breakfast clubs, curriculum review, and ending private school VAT exemptions.

## Immigration and Security

A Border Security Command will replace the Rwanda scheme. Additional asylum caseworkers and a returns enforcement unit will be established. Work visa policy will link to domestic skills training requirements.

## Crime and Justice

Neighbourhood policing will be restored with new officers. Knife crime measures include youth intervention programmes and weapon bans. Violence against women receives dedicated resources including specialist rape units in every police force.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers will lose voting rights. A mandatory retirement age of 80 applies to Lords members. Voting age drops to 16. Devolution will be strengthened with improved intergovernmental structures.

## Foreign Policy

NATO commitment remains central. The party seeks improved EU relations without rejoining the single market or customs union, including veterinary agreements and professional qualification recognition. Ukraine support continues.
